title: UFO Endless Runner — Gameplay Identities
approach: Ten sequential art-direction studies. Each prompt responds to a critique of the previous frame. Rationales describe design intentions; observed notes record what the resulting still actually demonstrates.

frames.name: crop-circle-pop
frames.title: Crop Circle Pop
frames.appeal: A bright, mischievous invasion with a visual hook that belongs specifically to UFOs: the ship leaves a crisp crop-circle pattern as it harvests.
frames.fit: The flattened capture patch separates the active area from uncollected targets. Simple circular canopies, short silhouettes and an open route support fast scanning.
frames.distinctive: The whole shape system grows out of concentric circles: saucer, hats, cow bellies, crop patterns and acquisition rings. It is a coherent UFO identity rather than another toy material.
frames.improvement: Start with a clean gameplay state, remove the permanent upgrade tray, reduce decorative farm assets and make capture feedback part of the ground.
frames.risk: Keep decorative crop rings near the edges so they cannot be confused with the live capture radius.
frames.production: Reusable low-poly meshes, one matte material atlas, a scrolling terrain atlas and a masked ground decal for flattened crops.
frames.style: ART DIRECTION — CROP CIRCLE POP. Very graphic circular low-poly design, almost like a boldly designed 3D arcade board. Mostly quiet pale PISTACHIO field with thick dark PLUM circular tree tops at boundaries, a few small BUTTER-yellow circular hay stacks and tiny CORAL roof rectangles cropped at edges. No standard green realistic farm, no lake or barn-centered composition. The player saucer is a small glossy cobalt disc with three odd mint lamps and a tiny off-center dome. Humans are huge flat mustard hat discs over small navy bodies. Cows are comically wide pear-shaped cream bodies, black spots and very small heads; sheep scalloped round puffs, pig a coral bean. Mostly matte flat-shaded geometry, a single short directional shadow, almost no texture. A clearly visible small capture footprint beneath the UFO flattens grass into a simple mint/cream concentric crop-circle stamp; ONE older faint decorative crop-circle remnant near upper edge, never competing with active circle. Tiny farmer hat spirals separately during abduction and small cow is upside down. Large empty pale pistachio playfield ahead, road only along edge. Navy tank/jeep use red angular warning chevrons. Economy of shapes and purposeful color roles, no generic glossy dashboard. HUD small clean navy capsules at top. Normal gameplay state: NO bottom upgrade tray, NO big cards, the lower terrain remains playable. Visually distinctive, charming, restrained, feasible as a polished real-time mobile game.

Use case: stylized-concept. Deliver ONE finished 9:16 portrait mobile-game gameplay style frame, full bleed. A buildable top-down UFO abduction endless runner on Earth. Real play scale: UFO about 9% of screen width, collectible humans/animals about 3–5%, wide readable navigable ground ahead. Camera looks vertically down: top of hats, roofs, vehicles and saucer; no sky, horizon, side view or isometric showcase. Everything in focus. Humorous simplified reusable low-poly 3D meshes and modest real-time lighting/shaders, no photorealism or elaborate diorama.
A small UFO moves toward screen top from lower-middle; a clear ground-plane capture circle and two CURVED DOTTED PATHS pull a tiny funny cow and flailing human toward it. NO visible tractor cone. Scattered human and animal targets ahead, including distinct cows, sheep and pig. One small military jeep from left and a tank from top threaten it with clearly telegraphed orange-red fire. One small bright laser intercepts a missile. No gore. Shapes distinguish friendly targets and hostile vehicles independently of color. Minimal quiet repeated ground modules; frame the route with a few small props, do not fill the middle with decorations. Top safe-area HUD: compact "12,480", "LV 07", XP meter, three shield pips, adapted to the visual world. No title/logo/watermark/phone frame or explanatory captions.
frames.observed: The frame has a clearer uncluttered playfield and a recognisable crop-circle trace. Its meadow and toy-like cast still feel close to earlier farm directions.
frames.next_test: Test the crop-circle stamp in motion and make the active capture radius consistently distinct from old traces.

frames.name: sleepy-suburbia
frames.title: Sleepy Suburbia
frames.appeal: A gentle late-night domestic comedy: a bizarre visitor interrupts an otherwise ordinary sleeping neighbourhood.
frames.fit: Quiet dark streets leave room for the saucer and targets to read. Warm window rectangles establish houses without demanding detailed environment models.
frames.distinctive: Bathrobe silhouettes, slippers, small home gardens and an incongruous cow shift the identity away from another farm-toy landscape.
frames.improvement: Retains the first frame's uncluttered playfield and clean HUD, but changes the world, character wardrobe, lighting and comic situation.
frames.risk: Night colours need testing on a dim phone; only the background should become subdued, never the collectible silhouettes or missiles.
frames.production: Short modular street segments, a small set of roof planes, reusable civilian bodies with robe/hat variations, baked-looking lighting plus local effects.
frames.style: ART DIRECTION — SLEEPY SUBURBIA. This image must look dramatically different from a green farm toy scene. A 1950s sleepy cul-de-sac at blue hour, rendered as sleek angular low-poly cartoon graphics with flat two-tone cel shadows, not photographic materials. Ground is mostly wide DUSTY LAVENDER asphalt and pale powder-blue pavement, roof-only coral and blue suburban houses clipped at screen edges, tiny mustard warm window shapes. No barn, crop field, hay, lake or trees filling edges. Wide open street and front-yard passage runs vertically through middle. Small human targets in nightcaps, pear-shaped bathrobes and enormous slippers, humorous stretched triangular bodies; hatlike nightcaps visible overhead. Few tiny animals: cream wide-bodied cow with tiny horns absurdly wandering the road, sheep and pig on nearby lawn strips. UFO is small milk-white flattened capsule-disc with coral dome, one mint lens underneath, a bright clean mint circular light footprint on asphalt. Abducted robe-wearing person rotates with dangling slippers and detached nightcap; cow gently tumbles. Earth silhouettes long and crooked rather than round toy blobs. Military jeep and tank are small sharply angular crimson-purple shapes at upper edges with distinct coral chevron warnings. Clear simple orange projectile and short mint laser. Mood tender, weird and quietly comic, no horror. Nearly textureless matte forms, deliberate theatrical warm/cool colour blocking, very short shadows to protect target visibility. Highest visual clarity belongs to actors and capture effect. Clean small cream HUD top, no bottom card tray. Direct top-down camera sees street plans, roof planes and top of nightcaps, never horizon or building fronts. All targets small at practical gameplay zoom.

frames.name: elastic-stampede
frames.title: Elastic Stampede
frames.appeal: The abduction itself is the joke: otherwise solid characters stretch into absurd, readable poses before popping into the ship.
frames.fit: A simple stretch-and-recoil motion can mark capture progress while a stationary circle shows range. The terrain stays quiet during the busiest action.
frames.distinctive: Rigid angular scenery contrasts with long, elastic animal and human silhouettes. The idea is an animation language, not a new surface finish.
frames.improvement: Builds on frame 2's situational humour by making the recurring player action funny even without the setting.
frames.risk: The stretch must leave the animal recognisable and must not hide incoming missiles. A still frame cannot establish how satisfying the motion feels.
frames.production: A handful of low-poly skinned characters or controlled mesh deformation, simple stretched capture poses, rigid modular props and a restrained unlit/cel shader.
frames.style: ART DIRECTION — ELASTIC STAMPEDE. A bold, peculiar low-poly cartoon game whose identity is absurd elastic silhouettes, NOT round chibi toys. Long-limbed farmers with extremely small heads under big flat hats, giant bean boots and bendy ribbon-like arms; cows have huge tapered teardrop rear ends, tiny narrow snouts, very wide paddle ears and skinny flexible legs. Sheep elongated scalloped sausages on tiny feet, pigs short bent beans. These must be original designed character proportions, not standard cute farm assets. Render with broad flat cel-shaded polygons, NO detailed material texture. World is geometrically rigid and sparse: PINKISH CORAL open ground, pale lilac path along one edge, a few deep-teal angular hedge wedges and mint roof rectangles at boundary, no generic green farm. UFO small cream asymmetric disc with a small teal glass bump and one funny crooked antenna, extremely simple. During capture the cow's body gently stretches into a curved teardrop and tiny legs flail; farmer's boots trail behind a bendy stretched torso and hat floats beside, comic rather than painful. Clear mint circular field on ground and dotted paths, no cone, no liquid melting or horror. One narrow bright laser and ONE orange missile, tank and jeep simple tiny deep navy wedge toys with huge coral warning chevrons. Colour-blocked, punchy, clean, slyly funny; broad silhouette contrast between stretchy cast and hard scenery. Small cream top HUD, no bottom upgrade tray, vast open play space, small objects at normal gameplay scale. Direct overhead game view; do not use giant close-up characters or a hero illustration.

frames.name: alien-field-guide
frames.title: Alien Field Guide
frames.appeal: Dry, curious alien science: collecting a cow is treated with the seriousness of cataloguing a rare specimen.
frames.fit: Small brackets identify the two active capture targets, a segmented ring shows progress, and the rest of the scene stays visually subdued.
frames.distinctive: Warm organic specimens sit inside a cool technical model of Earth. The identity comes from an alien observer's visual language rather than the toys' material.
frames.improvement: Carries forward the stronger actor silhouettes from frame 3 while using controlled colour and interface marks to reduce action clutter.
frames.risk: Too many brackets and numbers could turn a playful game into a dashboard. Limit annotation to the active targets.
frames.production: Simple flat-shaded meshes, one subtle outline pass, a few reusable UI brackets and ring graphics, muted modular terrain.
frames.style: ART DIRECTION — ALIEN FIELD GUIDE. A sophisticated, funny, radically restrained low-poly specimen-survey game. Most of Earth is a cool SLATE-GREY / BLUE-GREY miniature plan with only subtle flat shading, thin dark outlines, off-white roads and modest grey roof rectangles. NOT a radar wireframe, not a toy diorama. No colourful trees or busy grass: isolated low-poly slate shrub shapes and sparse ordered crop strips near edges. Collectible living humans and animals alone have warm SALMON, cream and ochre colours: pear-body white cows with salmon noses and tiny black patches, scalloped cream sheep, salmon pig, tiny lanky humans with broad ochre overhead hats. Small alien UFO is a smooth IVORY lens-like circle with dark blue glass centre and a small turquoise scanning fin. Two active capture specimens have minimal cream corner brackets plus a single geometric glyph each, NO extra written annotations or dense data. Capture circle is an elegant thin segmented turquoise ring on ground; two tiny dotted paths lead warm small cow and flailing hatless human toward saucer. The humour is absurd scientific seriousness applied to wonky little farm creatures, no printed jokes. Military enemies are angular charcoal objects with VERMILION chevrons and a single matching missile. Color and shape roles extremely disciplined. Top HUD tiny compact typeset cream numerals and mint XP meter. Show a level-up choice moment: exactly three restrained ivory upgrade tiles along bottom 12%, icon plus word "BEAM", "LASER", "SHIELD"; no stars, currencies, gauges or ornamental glow. Fresh map design with a broad diagonal white country road only across upper third and two roof rectangles at lower edges. Nearly vertical top-down camera and small game-scale actors, usable open space everywhere. No photographed materials, no craft grain, no pixel art.

frames.name: umbrella-panic
frames.title: Umbrella Panic
frames.appeal: A warm, slapstick street scene: umbrellas tip inside-out and belongings float away when the saucer passes.
frames.fit: Broad umbrella shapes make civilians readable from overhead. Empty road sections provide the runner's route, with props and buildings kept at the sides.
frames.distinctive: Rainwear, umbrella silhouettes, simple puddles and an ordinary town disrupted by stray livestock give it a different cast and spatial rhythm.
frames.improvement: Retains frame 4's selective target emphasis but restores character warmth and uses everyday objects as comic animation props.
frames.risk: Glossy puddles and multiple bright umbrellas could compete with warning effects. Keep reflections simple and use threat chevrons as well as colour.
frames.production: Modular streets, roof-only buildings, umbrella/civilian variants, a flat puddle mask and short looping rain accents; no costly realistic reflections are required.
frames.style: ART DIRECTION — UMBRELLA PANIC. High overhead low-poly comic mobile game on a rainy small-town street in soft daylight, not nighttime. Quiet DESATURATED TEAL asphalt, flat pale stone curbs, buildings shown as simple roof rectangles clipped around edges, a few broad flat puddle shapes with ONE painted light reflection each, no rain particle clutter. Civilians have small long bean bodies in cream, ochre and dusty pink raincoats; exaggerated broad umbrella canopies in MUSTARD, ivory and muted CORAL create bold memorable overhead silhouettes. Keep umbrellas sparsely distributed so targets separate. The abducted civilian's umbrella flips inside-out like a flower with feet dangling; nearby cow is a funny fat low-poly wedge with small ears and black-white patches tumbling belly-up. Sheep compact clouds, one round pink pig, all surprisingly on the open town road. UFO tiny glossy VERMILION saucer with black dome and a cream rim, one oversized turquoise lens, whimsical but no face. Its live capture circle and two dotted trails are brilliant MINT and have clean generous space. Small angular dark navy military tank and jeep approach from upper street and left intersection; big white-orange chevron warnings and one orange missile distinguish them from umbrellas. One short mint laser interception. Shape grammar: smooth umbrella arcs and funny long limbs against rectangular street geometry; shallow flat cel-shaded 3D with slightly rubbery tactile raincoat surfaces, minimal textures, no cinematic realism. Street curves gently down right side rather than a symmetric central corridor. Slim cream top HUD, no bottom upgrade cards. No barns, hay, crop fields, or repeated tree-border framing. Plan-view camera, small game-size actors, at least 60 percent clean playable street.

frames.name: roadside-oddities
frames.title: Roadside Oddities
frames.appeal: A sun-baked roadside comedy with lanky locals, improbable livestock and exuberant miniature architecture.
frames.fit: Broad empty sand and a single road curve give the runner clean space. A few memorable landmarks could differentiate chunks without filling them with props.
frames.distinctive: Exaggerated wedge silhouettes, roadside architecture and a tightly limited desert palette create a specific place beyond the generic barn-and-paddock set.
frames.improvement: Keeps the situational character of frame 5 but replaces detailed streets with large quiet shapes and a more economical environment kit.
frames.risk: A novelty landmark should stay at the edge and remain an obstacle, not steal attention from the UFO or suggest a different core game.
frames.production: A small set of exaggerated buildings, flat terrain patches, stylised cow/human meshes and a single directional light; detail comes from silhouette rather than texture.
frames.style: ART DIRECTION — ROADSIDE ODDITIES. Extremely designed stylized LOW-POLY 3D desert-roadside comedy, broad angular silhouettes with a flat matte poster-like finish. Ground mostly quiet PALE APRICOT sand; one sweeping deep-RED road edge crosses far left then exits top, no busy markings. Deep PETROL-BLUE isolated wedge shrubs, bone-cream rock shapes. One tiny eccentric roadside diner/gas-station roof clipped at upper-right, architecture built of exaggerated tilted wedges with a small cow-shaped roof silhouette, no written signs or logos. No green farm or city street. Lanky local human targets with impossibly broad flat white hats, long narrow ochre torsos, huge square turquoise boots; cattle have outrageous long wedge snouts, broad skinny triangular backs and four tiny legs, black-and-bone-white patches; sheep compact faceted clouds, dusty-pink pig. Character shapes are the star, not surface materials. Small UFO looks like a glossy white lopsided spinning diner plate with coral glass centre, turquoise rim and a stubby bent laser. Active cow turns upside down, farmer's huge hat tumbles separately, two clean mint dotted paths and one thin ground-plane capture ring. Tiny military tank is a squat dark petrol wedge with a short trumpet barrel and red warning chevron, jeep is a low trapezoid with huge square tires; one high-contrast red-orange missile. Shadows short and hard, only two shade values per mesh, no grain, realistic plants, tiny grass or material clutter. Keep all actors small with large empty space to navigate. Clean ivory top HUD with red score accent; NO bottom upgrade cards. Near-vertical plan view, roof planes and top of hats visible, no horizon, no perspective illustration. A distinctive small-team mobile-game world, not a rendered tourist diorama.

Tiny military tank is a squat dark petrol wedge with a short trumpet barrel and red warning chevron, jeep is a low trapezoid with huge square tires; one high-contrast red-orange missile. Clean ivory top HUD with red score accent; NO bottom upgrade cards. Near-vertical plan view, roof planes and top of hats visible, no horizon, no perspective illustration. frames.observed: The exaggerated snouts, hats and boots give the cast a specific identity. Broad sand keeps the action open; the roadside landmark could be reduced further.
frames.next_test: Keep landmark detail at the edge and test the animal shapes at a smaller on-phone scale.

frames.name: thermal-mischief
frames.title: Thermal Mischief
frames.appeal: The player sees Earth through a strange alien sense, with warm little creatures standing out against a cold miniature world.
frames.fit: The target class has a strong value hierarchy; angular military silhouettes and distinct warning glyphs separate threats from living collectibles.
frames.distinctive: It uses solid low-poly volumes with a false-colour shader, rather than a neon material swap or wireframe radar aesthetic.
frames.improvement: Takes frame 6's silhouette economy further by controlling the entire world's information hierarchy through one consistent alien viewing rule.
frames.risk: The palette must not imply that every warm object is safe. Threat shapes, symbols and projectile silhouettes need to carry meaning without colour.
frames.production: The same small low-poly asset set with flat false-colour material assignments or a stylised ramp shader; no real thermal simulation is needed.
frames.style: ART DIRECTION — THERMAL MISCHIEF. A remarkably different ALIEN FALSE-COLOUR view of a solid low-poly 3D world. This is NOT wireframe radar, not neon cyberpunk, not a colourful toy farm. Ground and roof planes are nearly flat DEEP INDIGO, shrubs and paths read as sparse colder violet polygon shapes. All scenery extremely quiet and low contrast. Living targets have bold nested flat heat-colour bands across simple SOLID broad faceted bodies: cream-hot centres, pale lemon shoulders, peach/coral edges, without blur or realistic infrared noise. Exaggerated cow silhouettes have long wide paddle ears, fat teardrop bodies and little legs; sheep scalloped blobs, pig a short fat bean, humans very large overhead hat discs over tiny bodies, all small at gameplay zoom. NO delicate facial details or black-white patches required: use animal shape. The UFO is a small icy WHITE clean ring disc with black centre, luminous CYAN capture-radius circle and dotted trails. A tumbling cream cow and flailing warm human float near it with a detached hot-yellow hat. Military jeep and tank are cold almost BLACK chunky angular objects with giant red-orange double-chevron threat badges hovering just above them; missiles have clear arrowhead silhouette, dark body and white-orange exhaust. One tiny cyan laser. Keep warm target glows bounded to the low-poly meshes, NO large bloom halos. Distinct graphic 3D with flat banded shaders and almost no shadows, no realistic textures. Top HUD small cold-white technical numerals. Show a level-up moment with three small nearly black bottom tiles, simple cyan icons and white words "BEAM", "LASER", "SHIELD", bottom 12% only. Broad overhead open map, one barely-visible violet diagonal road across upper-left, empty central route, no buildings with visible fronts, no sky. Playfully weird scientific alien perception, absolutely usable at phone scale.

frames.name: shadow-play
frames.title: Shadow Play
frames.appeal: A sunny, graphic world where small awkward creatures cast wonderfully exaggerated silhouettes.
frames.fit: The actors remain simple and the ground remains calm. Stable directional shadows can convey height during abduction without adding particle effects.
frames.distinctive: Its identity is a relationship between small low-poly forms and deliberately stylised shadow graphics, rather than texture or a special material.
frames.improvement: Responds to frame 7's dark-background dependency with a bright palette and shape-based emphasis that can be read without luminous shaders.
frames.risk: Shadows must remain non-colliding visual cues and should not overlap active threat markers. Target silhouettes need to be readable without their shadows.
frames.production: Simple low-poly meshes, a fixed directional light and controlled stylised shadows or projected shadow sprites; no complex material system.
frames.style: ART DIRECTION — SHADOW PLAY. Extremely graphic art-directed top-down low-poly game in just a few large colour fields, like sculptural cut-shape poster design translated into real 3D gameplay. Flat pale PINK / PEACH open ground, matte CREAM cow bodies and sheep, MUSTARD human hats, DEEP BURGUNDY long clean hard-edged shadows. No grain, photo textures, leafy detail, realistic reflections, grass decoration or glossy toy finish. Tiny models have funny sculptural silhouettes: cow squat broad rectangle with huge semicircular ears and a tiny nose, humans tall thin pegs with vast disc hats and bean boots, sheep cream scalloped wedge, pig short rose bean. Each actor casts a deliberately slightly oversized clean burgundy shadow diagonally across ground, with funny ears and hats legible in shadow. Keep shadows separated rather than wall-to-wall clutter. A cow in capture tips belly-up, its offset shadow shows its height; farmer spins hatless, hat drifts separately. Small UFO smooth turquoise pebble-disc, one pale-yellow central dome and eccentric tiny antenna; mint ground-plane capture circle with high-contrast dark-teal outer dashed stroke and just two neat dotted paths. Military tank/jeep tiny angular BURGUNDY-and-CORAL forms with bright orange threat chevrons; laser pale turquoise with dark outline so it reads on pink, one coral missile. Landscape has only a few cream roof rectangles cropped at edges, flat mustard path ribbon at far left and four large burgundy geometric tree canopies around boundary. Near-vertical overhead camera, very little visible building wall. Normal gameplay, compact burgundy top HUD with cream lettering and mint XP, NO bottom upgrade cards. Restraint, strong negative space, simple shippable geometry, no isometric miniature showcase.

frames.name: crooked-county
frames.title: Crooked County
frames.appeal: Everything on Earth seems awkwardly assembled: crooked hats, lopsided cows and vehicles that look one wobble away from losing a wheel.
frames.fit: Asymmetric silhouettes could make small actors identifiable while a clean, consistent camera keeps their collision footprints understandable.
frames.distinctive: Earth is built from skewed wedges and off-centre details; the alien saucer is the only perfectly round, precise object. The visual contrast belongs to the invasion.
frames.improvement: Keeps frame 8's limited palette and simple rendering while shifting personality out of large shadows and into reusable model silhouettes.
frames.risk: Crooked forms still need clear bounds and recognisable species; visual eccentricity should not imply unpredictable hitboxes.
frames.production: A small low-poly mesh library with intentionally skewed proportions, one flat material palette, short shadows and a tiny shared expression atlas.
frames.style: ART DIRECTION — CROOKED COUNTY. A bizarre, confident CUBIST LOW-POLY mobile game world. Earth models all use deliberately skewed tapered wedges, tilted trapezoids, asymmetrical masses and off-centre painted details; no voxel cubes, no origami folds, no craft texture, no round toy blobs. A funny cow is a wide lopsided IVORY wedge-body with one oversized black paddle ear, a short sideways blunt muzzle and four mismatched little legs; pigs dusty salmon trapezoid-beans, sheep off-kilter cream scalloped slabs. Humans are tall skinny blue trapezoids with absurd crooked MUSTARD brim hats, tiny heads, one boot bigger than the other, clear simple two-dot painted features only if visible. Earth looks joyfully badly assembled, not damaged or horror. The UFO is contrasting PERFECTLY ROUND small WHITE disc with an exact cobalt circular dome and three neat turquoise lenses, mechanically precise in this wonky world. A crooked cow tumbles and long-legged human flails while tilted hat flies off. Ground almost flat very pale BUTTER / YELLOW with a few broad muted CORNFLOWER field patches, one narrow coral path along edge, little crooked teal roof shapes and sawtooth tree tops clipped at boundaries. NO realistic farm props, lush detailed grass, fences everywhere or standard generic barn assets. Military jeep/tank are skewed navy trapezoids, asymmetrical little wheels, one ridiculous short cannon and red chevrons, still immediately recognisable threats. Clean mint capture ring and only two dotted paths. Short, quiet shadows, flat two-shade polygon lighting, sophisticated warm/cool colour blocking. Small simple blue-and-cream top HUD, no bottom upgrade cards. Strict overhead play camera and normal small game objects, not a giant character lineup. Bold original shape grammar across the whole world.

frames.next_test: Push a few model silhouettes further off-centre, simplify the burst and preserve predictable collision bounds.

frames.name: the-great-vacuum
frames.title: The Great Vacuum
frames.appeal: The UFO itself becomes the comic star: an increasingly over-equipped flying vacuum collecting a small procession of bewildered Earth creatures.
frames.fit: An orderly, short capture spiral communicates absorption without a large beam cone. Visible ship attachments can make level-up progress tangible during play.
frames.distinctive: The identity is a specific player-machine silhouette and a repeatable capture choreography, bringing the abduction and upgrade systems into the artwork.
frames.improvement: Combines the earlier frames' quiet terrain, distinctive silhouettes and restrained threat marks, while moving the focus away from large interception bursts and toward the growing player ship.
frames.risk: Attachments and orbiting captures can hide the player footprint. Keep the base circle and forward heading clear, and cap simultaneous capture silhouettes.
frames.production: A small base saucer plus modular attachment meshes, a simple two-slot capture animation, flat matte environment models and one short readable effect per action.
frames.style:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE polished 9:16 portrait top-down gameplay style frame for a real mobile endless-runner UFO abduction game, called THE GREAT VACUUM here only as art direction; do NOT write a title in image.

This must be an independent composition, NOT another symmetrical V-shaped cow/farmer capture leading to a centre-bottom UFO shooting a giant explosion. Change the actual shape language and gameplay staging. Camera is vertically overhead like a playable game map, roofs and top of hats visible, no sky, horizon, side-scrolling panorama or isometric product showcase. All in focus. Actors small at normal gameplay zoom, clear open navigation space.

VISUAL THESIS: a wonderfully peculiar flying vacuum saucer is the player's recognisable main character, visibly modified by acquired upgrades. Small off-white low-poly disc saucer at lower-LEFT of screen, only about 12 percent width including attachments. A large eccentric sea-green circular glass intake/dome, a peach rim, one thick short CORAL laser attachment, one lopsided mint ring emitter and three comically uneven little stabiliser fins. It is a UFO, not a household appliance with a hose, no face or arms. Simple polished enamel on alien tech contrasts with matte low-poly Earth. The silhouette should be memorable from a thumbnail, playful and obviously modular, no busy greebles or metallic realism.

Capture depicted as one SHORT clockwise crescent/spiral around the RIGHT HALF of the saucer's clear mint ground-radius footprint: one tiny comically pear-shaped cream/black cow tumbling belly-up and one lanky hatless farmer are being drawn along that same orbit, a detached enormous hat midway between, all separate little silhouettes. Dashed mint arc connects them to intake. NO tractor beam cone, NO huge floating cow, NO pair of long symmetrical V trails. At most two active captures, rest of the field quiet. A tiny miniature cow pictogram just above intake indicates one successful capture, no text.

WORLD: Earth is soft irregular geometric terrain, mostly pale OATMEAL meadow with large dusty CORAL rounded field patches and dark SAGE irregular tree-top blobs clipped at far edges. Sparse shapes, zero detailed grass, no dirt-grain texture, no barn fences everywhere. One small quirky roof-only cream/red farmhouse clipped at upper-left, a broad curved dark-sage footpath across upper-right, open middle. Low-poly casts have bespoke silhouettes: cows over-wide teardrop bodies and tiny ears, farmer coats long and flared with huge flat hats and tiny bean boots, sheep squat scalloped discs, pigs little tilted rose wedges. Five or six tiny targets ahead to collect, not huge characters. Only one short hard shadow per model.

MILITARY: tank and jeep appear at upper-RIGHT and far-right edges, small dark sage angular vehicles with crisp CORAL double-chevron warning badges and a single red triangular missile approaching. A SHORT thin mint laser from attached cannon taps the missile with a tiny three-ray spark, NO large explosion, smoke cloud or long line crossing whole screen. Capture action and UFO have primary visual emphasis. Shapes clearly differentiate targets and threats.

HUD: compact dark-sage top bar with cream score "12,480", "LV 07", mint XP bar, three cream shield pips. Show level-up choice state with exactly three SMALL ivory upgrade chips across bottom 10 percent, bold simple pictograms echoing actual bolt-on parts and labels "BEAM", "LASER", "SHIELD". No oversized glossy dashboard, duplicate currencies or other words. At least 80 percent image is usable gameplay world.

ART: unusual, restrained, warm graphic 3D, simple reusable flat-shaded low-poly geometry, tactile matte-painted surfaces with no visible complex textures, joyful awkward creature proportions, precise smooth alien circle against loose Earth shapes. Feasible for small-team mobile real-time rendering. Full bleed, no phone mockup, branding, watermarks, style captions.
